name: Doge
blurb: Kabosu the Shiba Inu side-eyeing the camera, with "such wow, much amaze" in Comic Sans
title: Doge Meme: Meaning, Origin & the Real Dog Kabosu
description: Doge is a photo of Kabosu, a Japanese Shiba Inu, posted by her owner in February 2010, captioned in broken Comic Sans English. It peaked in 2013.
answer: Doge is a meme built on a photo of Kabosu, a Shiba Inu from Japan, giving the camera a sideways, raised-eyebrow look. Her owner, the kindergarten teacher Atsuko Sato, posted the photo on her blog in February 2010; by 2012 it spread on Tumblr and Reddit with colourful Comic Sans captions in broken English like "such wow" and "very amaze", and in late 2013 it became the meme of the year. Kabosu died in May 2024 at 18.

body: The classic image is a fluffy tan-and-white Shiba Inu sitting on a couch, paws crossed, looking sideways at the camera with raised eyebrows, as if she is a little suspicious of you. Around her float short phrases in bright Comic Sans: "wow", "such fluff", "much concern", "very scare".
The joke is the voice: an inner monologue of a dog with very limited English, built from "such", "much", "very" and "so" plus a word that does not fit, and a single "wow".

head: Date
Event
rows: The misspelling "doge" for "dog" appears in an episode of the web cartoon Homestar Runner.
Atsuko Sato posts photos of her rescued Shiba Inu, Kabosu, on her blog.
Doge images with Comic Sans captions spread on Tumblr and 4chan; Shiba owners start calling the dogs "shibes".
Doge floods Reddit and becomes Know Your Meme's top meme of 2013; in December The Verge confirms the dog is Kabosu.
Cheems, a chubbier Shiba with a lisp, appears on Reddit's dogelore; in 2020 "Swole Doge vs. Cheems" comparisons go viral.
Kabosu dies of leukemia at 18; her owner announces it on 24 May.

body: In 2014 Doge also won the Webby Award for meme of the year, and the city of Sakura in Chiba, Kabosu's hometown, later honoured her with a park bench monument (2023) and a manhole cover (2024).

ul: Doge-speak captions: "such homework, very tired, wow".
Swole Doge vs. Cheems: a buff Shiba representing the strong old days next to a small, weak Cheems for today.
Doge reaction image: the side-eye alone to show mild suspicion.
Ironic Doge comics ("dogelore"), with a whole cast of Shiba characters.

body: Doge is a classic, one of the best-known images on the internet. It peaked in 2013, came back in ironic forms around 2018 to 2020, and is still used as a reaction picture. Many people now know it simply as "the Shiba meme".

Kabosu was a real dog who lived a long, quiet life in Sakura, Japan, and her owner announced in December 2022 that she had leukemia. When she died in 2024, fans around the world posted tributes. Her owner kept the photos on her blog the whole time.

faq.q: What is the dog in the Doge meme called?
faq.a: Kabosu, a female Shiba Inu from Sakura, Japan. She was adopted from a shelter by Atsuko Sato in 2008.
It is a deliberate misspelling of "dog" that appeared in the cartoon Homestar Runner in 2005 and was later attached to the Shiba photos.
No. Kabosu died on 24 May 2024 at the age of 18, after being treated for leukemia.
